e:resource.e:content: Safety alert symbols found throughout this manual are used to call your attention to instructions involving your personal safety and the safety of others. Failure to follow these instructions can result in injury or death.

Les symboles d'alerte de sécurité présents dans ce manuel sont utilisés pour attirer votre attention sur les instructions qui impliquent votre sécurité personnelle et celle des autres. Le non-respect de ces instructions peut entraîner une blessure ou un décès.

Des symboles d'alerte de sécurité sont utilisés dans ce manuel pour attirer votre attention sur des instructions concernant votre sécurité personnelle ainsi que celle d'autrui. Le non-respect de ces instructions peut entraîner des blessures ou la mort.
Note the use of signal words, DANGER, WARNING, CAUTION, and NOTICE with safety messages. The appropriate signal word for each has been selected using the following guidelines:

Notez l'utilisation de mots de signal, DANGER, ATTENTION, PRÉCAUTION et AVIS avec des messages de sécurité. Le mot de signal approprié pour chacun a été sélectionné en utilisant les directives suivantes :

Veuillez noter l'utilisation des termes signalétiques DANGER, AVERTISSEMENT, ATTENTION et AVIS avec les messages de sécurité. Le terme signalétique correspondant à chacun d'eux a été choisi selon les principes suivants :

DANGER indicates imminently hazardous situation that, if not avoided, can result in death or serious injury. This signal word is to be limited to the most extreme situations typically for machine components which, for functional purposes, cannot be guarded.

DANGER indique une situation imminente et dangereuse qui, si elle n'est pas évitée, peut entraîner la mort ou des blessures graves. Ce mot de signal doit être limité aux situations les plus extrêmes généralement pour les composants de la machine qui, à des fins fonctionnelles, ne peuvent être gardés.

Le terme « DANGER » indique une situation dangereuse imminente qui, si elle n'est pas évitée, peut entraîner la mort ou des blessures graves. Ce terme signalétique doit être limité aux situations les plus extrêmes, généralement pour des composants de machines ne pouvant pas être protégés à des fins fonctionnelles.

WARNING indicates a potentially hazardous situation that, if not avoided, could result in death or serious injury, and includes hazards that are exposed when guards are removed. It may also be used to alert against unsafe practices.

ATTENTION indique une situation potentiellement dangereuse qui, si elle n'est pas évitée, peut entraîner un décès ou une blessure grave, et comprend les dangers qui sont exposés lorsque les gardes sont enlevés. Il peut également être utilisé pour alerter contre les pratiques dangereuses.

Le terme « AVERTISSEMENT » indique une situation potentiellement dangereuse qui, si elle n'est pas évitée, peut entraîner la mort ou des blessures graves, et qui comprend des risques lorsque les protecteurs sont retirés. Il peut également être utilisé pour mettre en garde contre les pratiques dangereuses.
CAUTION indicates a potentially hazardous situation that, if not avoided, may result in minor or moderate injury. It may also be used to alert against unsafe practices.

ATTENTION indique une situation potentiellement dangereuse qui, si elle n'est pas évitée, peut entraîner des blessures mineures ou modérées. Il peut également être utilisé pour alerter contre les pratiques dangereuses.

Le terme « ATTENTION » indique une situation potentiellement dangereuse qui, si elle n'est pas évitée, peut entraîner des blessures mineures ou modérées. Il peut également être utilisé pour mettre en garde contre les pratiques dangereuses.
NOTICE is used to address safety practices not related to personal safety.
AVIS est utilisé pour traiter les pratiques de sécurité qui ne sont pas liées à la sécurité personnelle.
Le terme « AVIS » est utilisé pour traiter de pratiques de sécurité non liées à la sécurité personnelle.

Wear clothing and personal protective equipment appropriate for the job. Wear steel-toed shoes when operating. Wear hearing protection when exposed to loud noises. Do not wear additional hearing impairment devices such as radio headphones, etc.

Portez des vêtements et des équipements de protection personnels appropriés pour le travail. Portez des chaussures à orteils en acier. Portez une protection auditive lorsque vous êtes exposé à des bruits bruyants. Ne portez pas d'appareils auditifs supplémentaires tels que des écouteurs radio, etc.

Portez des vêtements et de l'équipement de protection individuelle appropriés pour le travail. Portez des chaussures de sécurité à embouts d'acier lors de l'utilisation. Portez un protecteur auditif lorsque vous êtes exposé à des bruits forts. Ne portez pas d'autres appareils pour déficience auditive tels que des écouteurs radio, etc.
It is your responsibility to read and understand the safety messages in this manual. You are the key to safety. Safety is your responsibility.
Il est de votre responsabilité de lire et de comprendre les messages de sécurité dans ce manuel. Vous êtes la clé de la sécurité. La sécurité est votre responsabilité.

Il est de votre responsabilité de lire et de comprendre les messages de sécurité contenus dans ce manuel. Vous êtes vous-même la clé de toute question de sécurité. La sécurité est de votre responsabilité.
This is a safety-alert symbol. When you see this symbol on your machine or in this manual, be alert to the potential for personal injury.
Ceci est un symbole d'alerte de sécurité. Lorsque vous voyez ce symbole sur votre machine ou dans ce manuel, soyez alerté sur le risque de blessure corporelle.
Ceci est un symbole d'alerte de sécurité. Lorsque vous voyez ce symbole sur votre machine ou dans ce manuel, faites attention aux risques de blessures corporelles.
Follow recommended precautions and safe operating practices.
Suivez les précautions recommandées et les pratiques d'exploitation sûres.
Respectez les précautions recommandées et les pratiques d'utilisation sécuritaires.
Replace missing or damaged safety signs. See the machine operator's manual for correct safety sign placement.
Remettez en place des panneaux de sécurité manquants ou endommagés. Consultez le manuel de l'opérateur de la machine pour connaître le bon placement du panneau de sécurité.
Remplacez les panneaux de sécurité manquants ou endommagés. Consultez le manuel d'utilisation de la machine pour connaître le bon emplacement des panneaux de sécurité.
Use caution when connecting, disconnecting, charging, and jumpstarting the machine's battery.
Soyez prudent lorsque vous branchez, débranchez, rechargez et redémarrez la batterie de la machine.
Keep sparks and flames away from the battery. Battery gas can explode and cause serious injury.
Éloignez les sources d'étincelles et de flammes de la batterie. Le gaz de la batterie peut exploser et causer des blessures graves.
Remove jewelry that can make electrical contact and create sparks.
Retirez les bijoux pouvant établir un contact électrique et créer des étincelles.

Chemicals used in agricultural applications can be harmful to personal health and/or the environment if not used correctly. Always follow all label directions for effective, safe, and legal use of any chemicals.

Les produits chimiques utilisés dans les applications agricoles peuvent être nocifs pour la santé personnelle et/ou l'environnement s'ils ne sont pas utilisés correctement. Suivez toujours toutes les instructions figurant sur l'étiquette pour une utilisation efficace, sécuritaire et légale de tout produit chimique.
ANHYDROUS AMMONIA IS AN INHALATION HAZARD AND WILL CAUSE SERIOUS INJURY OR DEATH. USE EXTREME CAUTION WHEN HANDLING IT OR PERFORMING ANY MAINTENANCE ON EQUIPMENT USED FOR ANHYDROUS AMMONIA.
Before performing any installation, repair or maintenance please follow the instructions below:

Only trained and certified personnel should work with anhydrous ammonia. If you are not, please seek out the appropriate agricultural department to attend a class to obtain the proper training and certification.
Wear appropriate safety goggles, gloves and breathing apparatuses.
Always know which way the wind is blowing.
Drain all tanks, hoses and piping of anhydrous ammonia COMPLETELY before removing, installing, performing maintenance or repairing any equipment.
Always remove device from service before performing any maintenance or repair.
Obey all local, state and federal laws regarding the handling of anhydrous ammonia.

Anhydrous ammonia is an important source of nitrogen fertilizer for crops. The improper handling of anhydrous ammonia can have catastrophic results on both plants and farm workers. Common injuries are severe burns to eyes, skin and the respiratory tract.

Always wear personal protective equipment (PPE). Standard PPE should be non-vented goggles, rubber gloves with thermal lining, face shield or an approved respirator. Wear a lightweight rubber suit, or (at the very least) a long sleeve shirt and coveralls.
Make sure anhydrous ammonia tanks are not filled beyond the recommended capacity.
Use care when handling the hose end valve so that it does not open accidentally. Do not move the hose by handling valve handle.
Be sure to bleed the hose coupling before disconnecting. Use care when cleaning plugged knives as anhydrous ammonia could be built up behind the plug.
Use emergency water supply for at least 15 minutes if exposed to anhydrous ammonia and then seek emergency medical attention.
Always carry a small squeeze bottle of fresh water.
Never assume NH₃ lines are empty, including the lines connected to the Torpedo.
Make sure the system is completely drained of NH₃. It can hide in low areas of the system. Look for frost on the hose or equipment. Frost usually indicates the presence of NH₃.
Always use high pressure hose when ammonia can be trapped in that segment, such as between the tank and the Torpedo.
Any place that has a high pressure hose should also have a hydrostatic relief valve and a bleed valve.
Always handle valves by the body and not by the wheel or latch.
Always make sure you are upwind of potential NH₃ release points.
When you park, position NH₃ equipment downwind from dwellings, people, and livestock.
Close the valve on the tank when you stop.
The first treatment for anhydrous ammonia exposure is WATER.
Wind direction is known and allows safe operation.
Hoses and other dated components are within their approved service life.
Fittings, valves, and connections are clean and free from rust.
Low-pressure tubes are free from leaks.
Application knives are free from obstructions.
Nurse tank is secured with a locking hitch pin.
Pressure relief valves are operating correctly.
Nurse tank has five gallons of fresh water.
PPE is available and being worn.
Ensure emergency water is immediately available.
Verify wind direction and stay upwind.
Park away from buildings, livestock, and people.
Close the valve on the NH₃ tank and follow bleed-down procedures.
Verify the tank valve is fully closed.
Disconnect the nurse tank supply hoses.
Open all bleeder valves on the cooler and the rest of system.
Check any hoses that have a low loop in them.
After completing bleed-down procedures, loosen fittings slowly and cautiously to verify that no residual pressure or trapped ammonia remains before service is performed.
Turn the Master valve on and leave it on during bleeding.
FOLLOW THESE INSTRUCTIONS WHEN APPLYING ANHYDROUS AMMONIA OR SERVICING EQUIPMENT.

Become familiar with all bleeder-valve locations on the NH₃ system before performing service. Multiple bleed points may be present throughout the system, and all trapped-pressure sections should be relieved in accordance with approved bleed-down procedures.
Before performing maintenance on the toolbar or equipment:

Please follow all of the instructions in this manual carefully and read the entire manual completely. Failure to do so may cause the product to function improperly or fail causing serious injury or death.

Anhydrous ammonia is a colorless non-flammable liquefied gas. Its vapor is lighter than air and has the same pungent odor as household ammonia. Although ammonia vapor is lighter than air, the vapors from a leak may hug the ground appearing as a white cloud. Chemically, ammonia is 82% nitrogen (N) and 18% hydrogen (H) and has the chemical formula NH₃. Ammonia by weight is 14 parts nitrogen to 3 parts hydrogen, or approximately 82% nitrogen and 18% hydrogen.

The definition of anhydrous is without water. Whereas household ammonia is 95% water, anhydrous ammonia has no water. Ammonia is so hygroscopic (water loving) that one cubic foot of water will dissolve 1300 cubic feet of ammonia vapor making water the primary weapon for first responders. Ammonia weighs 5.15 pounds per gallon in contrast to water which weighs 8.33 pounds per gallon. Since ammonia is so soluble in water there will be no layering effect when liquid ammonia is spilled into a surface water body. Booms, pads, sweeps and pillows that are usually used to contain and recover petroleum are ineffective on spills of ammonia into surface water.

Ammonia is a non-flammable gas but will ignite at a temperature of 1204°F within vapor concentration limits between 15% and 28%. (Paper ignites at 450°F, coal at 750°F.) Outside conditions that would support these vapor concentrations are very rare.
Ammonia will corrode galvanized metals, cast iron, copper, brass, or copper alloys. All ammonia piping, valves, tanks and fittings are constructed of steel.
Liquid ammonia boils at any temperature greater than –28°F and will expand to 850 times its liquid volume. One gallon of liquid will expand to 850 gallons or 113 cubic feet of gas.
Keep this important information in mind when working with NH₃

Ammonia appears in nature as a natural substance that results from decomposition. Ammonia vapor is a colorless gas with a pungent odor. Ammonia exists as a vapor at atmospheric conditions. Ammonia vapor is lighter than air and tends to rise when released to atmosphere.

Liquid ammonia released to atmosphere forms a white smoke by freezing the moisture in the air. Liquid ammonia has a very high coefficient of expansion with temperature. One gallon of liquid ammonia weighs approximately 5.15 lbs.; however the weight varies with temperature. When liquid ammonia reaches a temperature between its melting and critical points, it exerts a vapor pressure that increases with temperature. A closed container of liquid ammonia is in equilibrium with ammonia vapor and the container pressure bears a definite relationship to the temperature.
Boiling point is –28°F. Ignition point is 1,204°F.

Ammonia is stored and transported as a liquid under pressure. The pressure on the tank is the vapor pressure and remains the same whether the tank is 10% full or 80% full. This pressure is dependent on the temperature of the NH₃. The maximum filling level of an anhydrous ammonia tank is 85%.
Anhydrous ammonia is classified by the DOT as a non-flammable gas. Ammonia vapor is flammable over a narrow range of 15% to 28% by volume in air and a strong ignition source must be present.
Sentinel® is an ISOBUS-compatible control and monitoring platform for NH₃ application systems. It provides:

Rate Control: Sentinel Rate Control serves as the primary rate controller for the implement. The ECU monitors machine speed and system performance data and adjusts output to maintain the target application rate.

Row Monitoring: Sentinel Row Monitoring tracks application performance at each row to identify flow variations, restrictions, and blockages. The system utilizes solid-state electromagnetic flow measurement technology to capture flow data without moving parts.
The illustration below shows an overview of the plumbing for a Sentinel system for NH₃.
Precision Metering and Application of Anhydrous Ammonia
Accurate application of anhydrous ammonia (NH₃) requires a metering and control system that measures and regulates product flow under varying operating conditions.

Accurate metering of anhydrous ammonia is difficult with conventional variable-orifice metering systems. NH₃ is stored and transported as a liquid and must be maintained either below its boiling point of -28°F (-33°C) or under sufficient pressure to remain in a liquid state. When the temperature rises above -28°F, a portion of the liquid ammonia vaporizes and becomes gas.

Most application equipment relies on nurse tank pressure to move NH₃ through the delivery system and into the soil. As tank pressure increases or decreases, the amount of ammonia flowing through the system changes accordingly. Unless continuous adjustments are made, fluctuations in tank pressure can result in application rates that differ from the intended target rate.

Anhydrous ammonia presents additional metering challenges due to its rapid expansion when transitioning from liquid to vapor. When released to atmospheric pressure, liquid NH₃ expands to approximately 850 times its original volume. As ammonia travels from the nurse tank through the delivery system, a portion of the liquid continuously vaporizes, causing the ratio of liquid to vapor to change throughout the flow path.

Approximately 1% of the liquid ammonia may vaporize between the tank withdrawal tube and the metering point. Although this percentage appears small, the resulting vapor occupies a significant volume within the delivery system. At a tank pressure of 100 PSI, the vapor may occupy approximately 25% to 30% of the meter chamber volume. At 50 PSI, vapor can occupy more than 60% of the chamber volume. These variations make it difficult for conventional systems to meter and distribute NH₃ consistently and accurately.
The SurePoint Torpedo™ NH₃ System improves anhydrous ammonia application through flow conditioning and automated rate control.
Application accuracy depends on eliminating vapor-related measurement errors and compensating for changes in ground speed and tank pressure.

The Torpedo™ system utilizes a heat exchanger to convert NH₃ to a fully liquid state prior to metering. By delivering 100% liquid ammonia to the flow meter, the system enables precise flow measurement and accurate rate control. The controller and control valve automatically adjust for changes in ground speed to maintain the target application rate. Automatic control compensates for changing conditions and reduces misapplication.
A system capable of delivering the required flow rate at 90°F may not provide sufficient flow at 40°F if key components are improperly sized. Factors affecting system performance include:
NH₃ delivery hose size and configuration
The SurePoint Torpedo™ system is engineered with properly matched components to ensure reliable product delivery across a wide range of operating conditions and application rates.

After accurate metering has been achieved, maintaining uniform row-to-row distribution becomes the next critical challenge. The manifold system plays a key role in ensuring consistent product distribution across all application rows. In addition to affecting distribution accuracy, improperly designed manifolds may create flow restrictions in high-rate applications.

The SurePoint Torpedo™ system utilizes industry-leading Continental 360 Series Manifolds and Continental Vertical Dam Manifolds to provide consistent distribution and minimize flow restrictions, helping maintain uniform application across the implement width.
Challenges of Conventional NH₃ Metering Systems
In high-volume applications, with wide implements, higher operating speeds, or colder operating temperatures, component sizing is critical to maintaining adequate flow capacity.
This section provides information on installing your Sentinel NH₃ system.
Follow these guidelines for a safe, reliable install:
Inspect all components for shipping damage before installation.
Use Schedule 80 forged steel fittings on all high-pressure NH₃ plumbing.
Use approved thread sealant such as Reactoseal #5.
Install hydrostatic relief valves in any section where liquid NH₃ can become trapped.
Use NH₃-approved high-pressure hose wherever pressure can be trapped.
Use EVA tubing only on low-pressure discharge applications and vapor discharge lines.
Install only components approved for anhydrous ammonia use. For installation assistance or application-specific requirements, contact your authorized SurePoint dealer or SurePoint Technical Support.

Select components capable of supplying the required NH₃ flow under anticipated operating conditions. Withdrawal valves, ACME fittings, supply hoses, breakaway couplers, heat exchangers, splitters, and manifolds should be sized according to application rate, implement width, operating speed, and expected tank pressure. Refer to for sizing calculations and component selection guidance.
Verify the nurse tank is equipped with the correctly sized withdrawal valve for the desired flow rate. See for information on calculating your flow rate.
Install the globe valve assembly onto the nurse tank connection.
Connect the high-pressure supply hose between the globe valve and breakaway coupler.
Keep supply hoses as short and straight as possible.
Minimize the use of elbows and restrictive fittings.
If dual tanks are used, install equal-length supply hoses.
Install emergency shutoff capability as required.
Route hoses to prevent kinking or interference during turns and transport.
Install bleed valve discharge hoses. Route discharge lines to safely direct NH₃ vapor away from the operator and service areas.

The flow capacity of the supply system is limited by the lowest-capacity component in the product path. Verify that withdrawal valves, ACME fittings, hoses, breakaway couplers, and associated plumbing are appropriately sized for the required application rate.
Mount the full-port breakaway coupler in accordance with Continental installation recommendations.
Install hydrostatic relief valves in available service ports.
Verify that the coupler is positioned to allow it to properly disconnect during an emergency separation event.
Ensure all acme connections are tightened according to manufacturer specifications.
Install a breakaway coupler to prevent system damage, NH₃ loss, and operator exposure during separation.

Install hydrostatic relief valves in trapped-pressure sections where liquid NH₃ can be isolated between closed valves or other components. These valves help protect system components from pressure increases caused by thermal expansion.
Confirm that the strainer magnet, if equipped, is pointed down.
Mount the Torpedo assembly securely to the toolbar.
Position the unit where it will not interfere with folding mechanisms or normal implement operation.
Ensure all safety labels remain visible after installation.
Install the NH₃ strainer upstream of the Torpedo cooler.
Secure mounting hardware according to torque specifications.
Install vapor discharge tubes supplied with the Torpedo.
If required, weld supplied vapor tubes to the implement according to manufacturer instructions.
Use equal-length EVA tubing for all vapor discharge lines.
Route vapor discharge hoses away from operators and service areas.
Install a variable dump orifice based on expected system flow.
The Torpedo heat exchanger stabilizes NH₃ pressure and state to ensure accurate metering.
Installing vapor discharge tubing of equal lengths provides consistent vapor flow and cooling performance across the heat exchanger.
Refer to Technical Resources for dump-orifice selection based on expected NH₃ flow rate and application conditions.
Install the NH₃ turbine flowmeter downstream of the Torpedo cooler.
Observe flow direction arrows during installation.
Ensure the flowmeter receives 100% liquid NH₃ from the heat exchanger.
Connect the flowmeter sensor harness to the Sentinel system.
Configure the Sentinel flow calibration value to 580 pulses per gallon.
To mount a standard A-360 Splitter:
Mount the splitter directly on the Torpedo assembly or remotely as required.
Verify adequate clearance for the full range of toolbar movement. Ensure the splitter, mounting brackets, hoses, and fittings do not contact fold points or moving components.
Install the correct outlet orifices before operation.
Use 1¼" high-pressure hose from Torpedo to splitter when section valves are installed.
Use 1" reinforced EVA hose when section valves are not installed.
Install a hydrostatic relief valve and bleeder valve at the remote splitter assembly. Route bleeder hoses away from operators and service areas.
Select splitter outlet orifices according to expected flow rate and operating conditions. Refer to Technical Resources for orifice selection guidance.
Remote splitter assemblies can create trapped-pressure sections. Install hydrostatic relief and bleeder valves as required to safely relieve pressure during service and thermal expansion events

When NH₃ stabilizer injection is used, install the SurePoint Injection Kit in accordance with approved application requirements. The assembly consists of an NH₃ mixing chamber, NH₃ check valve, stabilizer check valve, injection port, braided supply hose, hydrostatic relief valve, remote bleed valve, mounting brackets, and associated hardware.
Verify flow direction markings before operation.
Refer to for assembly breakdowns and replacement parts.
For systems using electric section control:
Install SurePoint electric shutoff valves between the splitter and manifold sections.
Use equal-length high-pressure hoses from splitter to all manifold sections.
1" hose for three sections or fewer
¾" hose for four or more sections
Mount valves in an accessible, protected location.
Connect valve wiring according to the Electric Section Valve Pinout in .
Equal-length hoses help maintain consistent pressure and flow distribution between manifold sections.
Mount section manifolds securely to the implement frame.
Position manifolds to avoid interference with fold points and moving components.
Install manifolds as evenly as possible across implement sections.
Connect equal-length EVA tubing from manifold outlets to knives.
Route tubing to prevent low spots where NH₃ can become trapped.
Ensure tubing lies flat during storage.
Verify total outlet counts match the row configuration.

Keep outlet counts as balanced as practical between manifold sections. Manifolds should generally be within one outlet of each other. For example, a 17-row implement may be divided into 6/6/5 outlets, but not 7/5/5.
Once the system has been plumbed to the manifolds, the final plumbing step is to run lines from the manifold distribution block to the knives at the individual rows. To complete installation:
Find the longest run from the manifold to the knife.
Determine the amount of hose required for that run.
Cut the hose for that run.
Cut additional hoses of equal length for all additional rows.
Attach the hose to the manifold hose barb and secure with a hose clamp.
Route the hose from the manifold to the row knife, ensuring plenty of slack at fold points.
Attach the hose to the knife at the row and secure with a hose clamp.
Secure the hose to the implement, again using care to ensure that it will not be pinched when the implement folds.

There are two hose bards on the side of the Torpedo to route NH₃ vapor. There are also two workpoint vapor hose connectors on the implement. If your implement doesn't have the necessary connectors, SurePoint can provide them. To install the vapor lines:
Measure the distance from the Torpedo to the furthest vapor placement connection at the row.
Cut the vapor hose to this size.
Cut a second, equal length of vapor hose.
Connect the hose to a the vapor connector on the Torpedo and secure with a hose clamp.
Route the hose to the row, ensuring it will not be pinched at fold points.
Connect the hose to a the vapor connector at the row and secure with a hose clamp..
Secure the hose to the implement, taking care that it is safe from pinching when the implement closes.
Bleeder hoses help ensure NH₃ vapor is exhausted away from personnel and service areas when bleeding the system. To install the bleeder hoses, for each bleeder valve:
Connect the hose to the bleeder location and secure with a hose clamp.
Route the hose to a safe location away from personnel and service areas, ensuring it will not be pinched at fold points.
Place the other end of the hose in a safe location.
Secure the hose to the implement, taking care that it is safe from pinching when the implement closes.
Once you have completed installation of all the NH₃ plumbing components, install the Sentinel ECU and harnessing components.
Whether you are using Sentinel for Rate Control, Row Monitoring, or Rate Control with Row Monitoring, the first step is to install the Sentinel ECU.

Install the ECU on your implement or tractor in a location where it will not interfere with operation. Use the provided bracket and bolts to mount the ECU. The bracket supports both vertical and horizontal mounting of the ECU. Note: When mounted vertically, the connector should point downward.ECUorientation
If necessary, route the provided ISO extension cable from the implement hitch to the desired Sentinel ECU mounting location.

Locate the 2-pin Molex power connector and the 12-pin Ampseal POWER/CAN connector or the 9-pin ISO connector that the Sentinel ECU will be connected to. These connectors are labeled. Remove the terminator.
Connect the harness connector labeled ECU to the Sentinel ECU.
Connect the other end of the harness to the Molex/Ampseal POWER/CAN connection.
Use the previously removed terminator to terminate the ISO OUT POWER/CAN connection found on the ECU harness.
After the ECU is installed, connect the harnessing to the Torpedo assembly.
Connect the PRESSURE harness connector to the pressure transducer on the Torpedo.
Connect the FLOWMETER harness connector to the flowmeter.
Connect the SERVO CONTROL harness connector to the servo valve.
Connect the MASTER valve connector to the master valve.
Once installation is complete and before using the system, verify:
All fittings are tightened and leak-free.
Relief valves are installed in trapped-pressure sections.
Bleeder valve hoses route vapor away from operators.
High-pressure hoses show no signs of twisting or kinking.
Equal-length distribution tubing is installed where required.
Flowmeter and sensors are connected properly.
Electrical harnessing is secured and protected.
Ensure the tank supply valve remains closed until startup procedures begin.
Vapor return tubing is installed, secured, and routed correctly.
When pressurizing a newly installed or serviced NH₃ system, ensure all personnel are in a safe location before opening the nurse tank valve and filling system components with NH₃.
Pressurize the system slowly through designated valves.
Avoid sudden pressure shocks to piping, hoses, gauges, and regulators.
Stop immediately and investigate any abnormal condition.
Verify proper operation of control valves, regulators, flow devices, and gauges.
Recheck connections after the system has stabilized under normal operating conditions.

Sentinel is accessed on in-cab displays as a virtual terminal (VT)/virtual implement (VI). Because Sentinel is ISOBUS-compliant, it can operate on a range of displays. Follow the instructions below to access Sentinel on your specific screen.
To access Sentinel on the John Deere Gen4 or G5 display:
Select ISO from the 4640 Home screen.
If you have more than one ISOBUS implement attached, it may be necessary to select ISOBUS Menu to open the ISOBUS selection list.
To access Sentinel on a John Deere 2630 display:
Sentinel should appear automatically on the Home screen of the 2630 after the initial connection.
It may take several minutes for Sentinel's interface to load the first time it is connected. Subsequent loading should be significantly faster.
To access Sentinel on a Pro 700 display:
Select Toolbox > Layout to tell the display to update the list of connected devices.
It may take several minutes for the display to find and load Sentinel's interface the first time it is connected. Subsequent loading should be significantly faster.
Select ISOBUS to display the list of ISOBUS devices or select Sentinel.
To access Sentinel on the Ag Leader InCommand:

SurePoint Technical Support has additional screenshot-based instructions for configuring displays to use Sentinel. This includes setting up Task Control, Section Control, Work Setup, and other options depending on display.

The 2630 display supports only one ISOBUS ECU when used with Task Control. Because of this, if using this display to control planter functions, task control functions like section control will not work with Sentinel.

e:resource.e:content: Select Installation Wizard to begin the configuration process.
The Product Configuration screen opens.Product Configuration
A sets the tractor to implement distance. This is the distance from the tractor hitch to the implement axle.
B configures implement offset if needed.
C sets the implement axle to workpoint distance.
Select Ground Speed if you are using GPS.
Select Wheel Speed to calculate speed based on wheel rotation.
Select Machine Selected Speed when using a separate, tractor-provided speed input.
Select ECU to select GPS input from the ECU, if installed.
Select Simulate Speed if testing/calibrating Sentinel.
Enter ECU Speed Calibration if using external GPS. The GPS manufacturer provides this value, usually on a sticker on the GPS receiver unit.ECU Speed Calibration
Enter Speed Smoothing Interval to smooth out speed reporting.
The Diagnostic panel displays which speed sources are reporting (only available when moving).
Select Use External Master Switch if you are using a foot pedal or other external switch to control Sentinel.
Select Use Height Switch to enable height switch sensing.
Select Setup to configure your height switch.
Select Enable Task Control if you are using Sentinel with Task Control.Task Control
The Product Rows and Sections screen opens.

e:content.emphasis: Configure rows and sections for this product:

e:resource.e:content: Verify that Total Rows is correct.
Num Rows shows the number of rows per section.

On initial setup, Sentinel calculates this and sets the number of rows per section by dividing the total rows by the number of sections. If this is not the correct configuration for your application, enter Num Rows for each section manually.
Enter the Total Rows for this product.
Enter the Total Sections for this product.
Enter the Row Spacing for your implement.

The following sections provide information on fine-tuning Sentinel NH₃ Rate Control. Begin with the recommended starting values and adjust settings as needed to optimize system performance for the application and operating conditions.

Control Speed (Ctrl Speed) determines how aggressively Sentinel adjusts the control valve to maintain the target application rate. The recommended starting value is 350. Adjust this setting as needed to optimize Rate Control performance. Observe system operation under normal field conditions and monitor the relationship between TARGET and ACTUAL application rates.
If rate response is slow when operating conditions change, increase Ctrl Speed incrementally. Increasing Control Speed increases response speed.
If the application rate fluctuates excessively or does not stabilize near the target rate, decrease Ctrl Speed incrementally. Reducing Control Speed may improve rate stability.
If the application rate changes greater than approximately 5% are observed during normal operation, reduce Ctrl Speed and reevaluate system performance.
After each adjustment, operate the system long enough to evaluate the changes before adjusting again.
To adjust control speed, from the Home screen:
Smoothing (Rate Smooth) affects how application-rate information is displayed. The recommended starting value is 10%. Adjust this setting as needed.
When the ACTUAL rate is within the configured smoothing percentage of the TARGET rate, Sentinel displays the ACTUAL rate as equal to the Target Rate.

A larger Rate Smooth value increases the range over which the ACTUAL rate is displayed as the TARGET rate. A smaller Rate Smooth value reduces that range. This setting affects rate display behavior only.

Proper component selection begins with determining the maximum NH₃ flow rate required by the application. Required flow is influenced by application rate, implement width, ground speed, and operating conditions. Use the capacity tables in this section to estimate the flow required by the system and to verify that major components are appropriately sized for the intended application.

All Torpedo models utilize the same Continental heat exchanger assembly. Differences between Models 100, 200, 250, and 300 are primarily related to supply-side plumbing size and component capacity necessary for higher-flow applications.

Ensure that all major flow-path components are capable of supplying the required flow rate. System capacity is limited by the lowest-capacity component in the product path. A properly sized system should be capable of achieving the required application rate under the lowest anticipated operating temperature and tank-pressure conditions.

After calculating required NH₃ flow rate, verify that all components can supply and distribute that flow under expected operating conditions. System performance is limited by the lowest-capacity component in the product path. A system that is properly sized at high tank pressures or warm temperatures may not have sufficient capacity during colder operating conditions.
System sizing is performed in three steps:
Calculate the required NH₃ flow rate based on application rate, implement width, and operating speed.
Select supply-side components capable of delivering the required flow, including the withdrawal valve, ACME fittings, supply hoses, breakaway coupler, and Torpedo system.
Size the distribution system based on the required flow per splitter outlet and manifold outlet. Use this information to select splitters, manifolds, section valves, and distribution hoses.
Use the following general process when selecting system components:
Calculate the required NH₃ flow rate using the formulas in .
Select a Torpedo system configuration capable of supplying the required flow.
Verify that the withdrawal valve, ACME fittings, supply hoses, and breakaway coupler support the required capacity.
Determine the required flow per splitter outlet and select the appropriate splitter configuration.
Calculate the required flow per manifold outlet and select the appropriate manifold model.
Verify that all sections of the system are sized to support the required application rate under anticipated operating conditions.

Component sizing should account for the most demanding expected operating conditions. Lower tank pressures, colder temperatures, wider implements, higher travel speeds, and higher application rates all increase system flow requirements. Components that perform adequately under favorable conditions may not provide sufficient capacity under peak demand conditions.
The components between the nurse tank and the heat exchanger have the greatest influence on overall system capacity. Pay particular attention to:

Restrictions in any of these components can limit product flow and prevent the system from achieving the target application rate, especially during high-rate, high-speed, or low-temperature operation.

Select a withdrawal valve whose rated capacity exceeds the calculated system flow requirement. System capacity is limited by the lowest-capacity component in the supply path, including the withdrawal valve, ACME fittings, hoses, breakaway coupler, and heat exchanger.
Supply hose from nurse tank to Torpedo
Size according to required system flow capacity
Keep hoses as short and straight as possible. Minimize elbows and restrictions.
Use equal lengths to maintain balanced flow from both tanks.

Used when electric section valves are not installed.

All hoses should be equal length.
Route tubing to avoid low spots and trapped NH₃.
Provides consistent vapor flow and cooling performance.

Select globe valve and ACME fitting assemblies with sufficient capacity to support the calculated NH₃ flow requirement. The entire supply-side plumbing system, including tank withdrawal valve, globe valve assembly, ACME connection, supply hose, breakaway coupler, and heat exchanger, must be sized as a matched system. Flow capacity is limited by the lowest-capacity component in the product path.

Select supply and distribution hoses with sufficient capacity to support the calculated NH₃ flow requirement. High-pressure hoses should be used in any portion of the system where NH₃ can be trapped under pressure, including the supply side of the system and section-controlled distribution circuits. Hose length should be minimized where possible to reduce pressure loss, and equal-length hoses should be used in parallel flow paths to maintain balanced product distribution.

Select a breakaway coupler with sufficient capacity to support the calculated NH₃ flow requirement. The breakaway coupler should be sized to match the supply-side plumbing and should not become a restriction in the product path. Full-port breakaway couplers are recommended to minimize pressure loss and maintain system performance during high-rate, high-speed, or low-temperature operation.

All Torpedo models utilize the same Continental heat exchanger assembly; differences between Models 100, 200, 250, and 300 are primarily related to supply-side plumbing size and component capacity necessary to support higher flow rates.

Select the correct orifice for your application using the following information.

Splitter outlet orifices maintain proper flow distribution between manifold sections. Install the correct size orifice before operation. Orifice selection is based on the expected flow rate through each splitter outlet.

The Torpedo heat exchanger utilizes a variable dump orifice to regulate the amount of NH₃ used for cooling. Select an orifice that provides sufficient cooling while minimizing the amount of product discharged through the vapor-return system.

Select an orifice small enough to minimize NH₃ discharge through the vapor-return system.
Select Orifice D only for applications requiring additional cooling or where N-Serve® treatment contributes to heat-exchanger fouling.

Manifold pressures greater than approximately two-thirds of tank pressure may restrict overall system flow. Manifold pressures below 30 PSI may reduce row-to-row distribution accuracy. Actual operating pressure will vary with application rate, operating speed, and tank temperature.

The flowmeter is factory calibrated to 580 pulses per gallon. Under normal operating conditions, no adjustment is required. Periodically verify flowmeter accuracy by comparing Sentinel totals to a known quantity of NH₃ consumed.

If a consistent measurement error is observed, calculate a new Flow Cal value using the following formula:
New Flow Cal = (Current Flow Cal × Displayed Volume) ÷ Actual Volume
Current Flow Cal = existing Sentinel Flow Cal setting
Displayed Volume = quantity reported by Sentinel
Actual Volume = independently measured quantity applied
Small variations may occur due to differences in measurement methods, tank inventory estimates, and operating conditions. Adjust Flow Cal only when a repeatable error is observed.
